[2026 São Toméan parliamentary election] Parliamentary elections were held in São Tomé and Príncipe on 27 September 2026. No party won an outright majority, with the MLSTP – Social Democratic Party winning a plurality of 24 seats out of 55 in the National Assembly. == Background == On 6 January 2025, president Carlos Vila Nova dismissed Prime Minister Patrice Trovoada and his government, citing Trovoada's prolonged absences and his government's failure to solve multiple issues. Trovoada responded calling his dismissal "illegal" and "unconstitutional". Vila Nova then selected then Minister of Justice, Ilza Amado Vaz, as prime minister. Vaz then resigned three days later on 12 January 2025, stating in a letter that her continued leadership "would not contribute to the success of public policies and the harmonious and peaceful development." Vila Nova thereafter picked Américo Ramos, who was not endorsed for the prime ministerial role by the ADI, being criticized for ignoring the majority of the National Assembly. In the presidential election held in July of the same year, Vila Nova was re-elected president over Nito Abreu, the candidate of ADI. That same month, the Constitutional Court issued a ruling recognizing the legitimacy of an extraordinary congress held by ADI in June at which Américo Ramos proclaimed himself the new leader of ADI. == Electoral system == Of the 55 members of the National Assembly, 53 are elected by closed list proportional representation in seven multi-member constituencies based on the seven districts. Overseas voters are grouped in two single member electoral districts (Europe and Africa). == Results == On 28 September, the National Electoral Commission announced that MLSTP won the election with 367 more votes than the ruling ADI, marking its first election victory since 2002.
